chromatic.constantStructure@1.1.summary: Slide into B♭7 with its own shape: C7 → B7 → B♭7, the whole hand moving together.
chromatic.constantStructure@1.1.deepDive:
With room for two, start a whole step above, as here: C7, B7, then B♭7.

Where else: Approaching any target chord on the final 1–2 beats of the preceding bar.

On the bandstand: Take the exact voicing of the upcoming target chord, shift your whole hand up 1 (or 2) half steps, and slide chromatically down into it.
chromatic.constantStructure@1.1.recreateRule: Near the end of a chord, play the next chord's exact shape a half step above it and slide the whole hand down.

functional.secondaryTwoFive@2.1.summary: Swap B♭7 for Gm9 → C7(♭9): a ii–V that walks you into F6.
functional.secondaryTwoFive@2.1.deepDive:
C7(♭9)'s ♭9, D♭, falls a half step to C, the 5th of F6.

Where else: Before any major or minor target chord (or solitary V7) with at least 2 beats.

On the bandstand: From the target chord, go up a 5th for V7 and another 5th (or a whole step above the target) for ii.
functional.secondaryTwoFive@2.1.recreateRule: Before any major or minor chord, go up a fifth for the V and another fifth for the ii.

dominant.tritoneSub@8.3.summary: Play A♭9 instead of D7(♭9). Same two tense notes, but the bass slides down a half step into Gm7.
dominant.tritoneSub@8.3.deepDive:
Every note of A♭9 is a tone or tension of D7(♭9): A♭ is the ♭5, E♭ the ♭9, B♭ the ♭13. So A♭ Lydian dominant and D altered share all seven notes: both are modes of E♭ melodic minor.

Where else: Any dominant 7th chord resolving down a perfect 5th.

On the bandstand: Keep your original V7 guide-tone shell (3rd & ♭7) and put the root a half step above the target chord.
dominant.tritoneSub@8.3.recreateRule: Over any dominant 7th resolving down a fifth, try the dominant 7th a half step above the target.

voicing.upperStructureBVI@8.3.summary: Over D7's shell, play the B♭ triad: one easy shape gives you D7(♯9,♭13).
voicing.upperStructureBVI@8.3.deepDive:
All three triad notes sit in D altered, so the right hand can keep going in that scale.

Where else: Any altered dominant 7th (especially V7 resolving to a minor chord).

On the bandstand: Hold a root–♭7–3 shell in LH; in RH play the major triad a major 3rd below the dominant's root.
voicing.upperStructureBVI@8.3.recreateRule: Over a dominant 7th, hold root, ♭7 and 3rd in the left hand and play the major triad on its ♭13 above.

gospel.halfStepTurnaround@10.1.summary: Turn C7 → F6 into B♭/C → G♭13(♯11) → F6/9: a slide into home from a half step above.
gospel.halfStepTurnaround@10.1.deepDive:
G♭13(♯11)'s ♯11 is C: the sub keeps C7's root inside, as the ♯11.

Where else: A V7 resolving to a major tonic with at least 2 beats.

On the bandstand: Play a major triad a whole step below V over the V bass, then plane a 13(♯11) chord from a half step above I down into home.
gospel.halfStepTurnaround@10.1.recreateRule: Before a major I, play IV/V, then a 13(♯11) chord a half step above I, and slide down into I.

modal.backdoorTwoFive@10.1.summary: Come home from below: B♭m7 → E♭9 → F6. Darker than C7, with no E leaning up into F.
modal.backdoorTwoFive@10.1.deepDive:
Where else: Replacing a V7 resolving to a major tonic.

On the bandstand: Play the minor 7th on the 4th degree of the target key, then drop the 7th to make the dominant a whole step below I.
modal.backdoorTwoFive@10.1.recreateRule: For a major I, play the minor 7th a 4th above it, then the dominant 7th a whole step below it.

dominant.mediantDominant@10.1.summary: Play A7(♭9) instead of C7: the same diminished shape on top, a new bass under it.
dominant.mediantDominant@10.1.deepDive:
A7 usually leads to Dm, so the ear expects D minor and gets F major instead.

Where else: Replacing a V7 that resolves to a major chord.

On the bandstand: Keep the right hand on the °7 a half step below I; put the bass a major 3rd above I instead of a 5th.
dominant.mediantDominant@10.1.recreateRule: Over V7 to I, keep the diminished 7th a half step below I and put the bass a major 3rd above I.
